subject: brain
topic: Your memory of your own life is a creative hallucination
angle: Human memories are not static recordings but are dynamic reconstructions that can be selectively rewritten, abolished, or distorted during a process called reconsolidation.
title: The Reconstruction of Memory

hooks.text: Is your memory a recording or a reconstruction?
You think your memories are static. They are actually dynamic reconstructions.
You are rewriting your own history every time you remember it.
A kitchen chair in a dim room.
Your memory is a creative hallucination.

reveal.headline: You can abolish a stable memory.
reveal.body: Interrupting the process of reconsolidation can remove a memory that was previously stable.

explain.headline: Memory is a reconstruction.
explain.body: Human memories are not static recordings. They are dynamic reconstructions. They can be rewritten, abolished, or distorted during a process called reconsolidation.

matters.headline: Your history is fluid.
matters.body: That may be why your past feels different each time you recall it. Your brain actively alters the information during the act of remembering.

example.headline: A childhood kitchen.
example.body: You remember the smell of toast and the color of the cabinets. Each time you think of it, your brain redraws the scene.

question.headline: Which part of your past is no longer real?

claims.text: Human declarative memory can be selectively rewritten during reconsolidation.
claims.quote: These results demonstrate that human declarative memory can be selectively rewritten during reconsolidation.

claims.text: Interrupting the reconsolidation process can abolish a previously stable memory.
claims.quote: Critically, interrupting this reconsolidation process can abolish a previously stable memory.

claims.text: Extinction during reconsolidation prevents the return of defensive reactions and diminishes PFC involvement.
claims.quote: These results suggest that extinction during reconsolidation prevents the return of defensive reactions and diminishes PFC involvement.

claims.text: Videos that were more surprising when interrupted produced more false memories.
claims.quote: We found that videos that were more surprising when interrupted produced more false memories.

claims.text: Individuals with PTSD, a history of trauma, or depression are at risk for producing false memories when they are exposed to information that is related to their knowledge base.
claims.quote: Our review suggests that individuals with PTSD, a history of trauma, or depression are at risk for producing false memories when they are exposed to information that is related to their knowledge base.

claims.text: Perception and memory are imperfect reconstructions of reality that can be influenced by several factors resulting in false memories.
claims.quote: Perception and memory are imperfect reconstructions of reality. These reconstructions are prone to be influenced by several factors, which may result in false memories.

verdict: The evidence shows that memories are labile reconstructions that can be actively altered or impaired during retrieval and reconsolidation.
caveat: The sources do not provide a comprehensive view of all memory stages, as most studies focus specifically on either encoding or retrieval.
caption:
Your memories are not permanent files. They are dynamic reconstructions that change every time you access them.

Research shows that memories can be rewritten, abolished, or distorted during reconsolidation. These findings focus specifically on encoding and retrieval rather than all memory stages.

How often do you notice your memories changing over time?
